# {{NAME}}: Documentation Standards

{{NAV}}

{{#single}}
> **Applies to:** `docs/` · **Generated by:** the [WanAware docs kit]({{KIT_HOME}}). Do not edit this file; change the standard in `wanaware/.github` and refresh.
{{/single}}
{{#monorepo}}
> **Applies to:** `docs/` and every `{{COMPONENTS_DIR}}/*/docs/` · **Generated by:** the [WanAware docs kit]({{KIT_HOME}}). Do not edit this file; change the standard in `wanaware/.github` and refresh.
{{/monorepo}}

This document defines how WanAware repositories are documented, so that every repository and every service is described the same way, and a reader who knows one set of documents can find their way around any other. It is the rulebook for writing and reviewing documentation in this repository. It is the same in every repository that uses the docs kit, apart from the parts that depend on the repository's layout ({{#single}}single service{{/single}}{{#monorepo}}monorepo{{/monorepo}}).

## 1. Principles

1. **One structure everywhere.** Every repository{{#monorepo}}, and every service in it,{{/monorepo}} has the same set of documents, with the same file names, titles and numbered sections.
2. **Code is the source of truth.** Every statement must be verifiable against the code in this repository. Defaults come from code, not from `.env` samples. When something is defined outside this repository (for example replica counts in `wanaware-infrastructure`), say so rather than guessing.
3. **One source of truth.** The numbered documents describe the system *as it is now*, and they are the only documentation maintained alongside the code. Decisions are recorded in `01-architecture.md`, proposals live in tickets and pull requests, and earlier documents live in git history ([§7](#7-earlier-documents-and-new-designs)).
4. **Explain once, link everywhere else.** Explain a concept in the most general place that owns it ({{#monorepo}}the repository-level `docs/` for anything shared by several services{{/monorepo}}{{#single}}the repository that implements it, for anything shared with other services{{/single}}) and link to it rather than repeating it.
5. **Diagrams as code.** Diagrams are Mermaid blocks inside the Markdown, so they are reviewed, diffed and rendered by GitHub like any other text.

## 3. The standard document set

| File | Title suffix | Covers | Required diagrams |
|---|---|---|---|
| `README.md` | Overview | Summary, at-a-glance table, responsibilities, position in the platform, documentation map, related documents | `flowchart LR` of direct neighbours |
| `01-architecture.md` | Architecture | System context, components, runtime flows, concurrency, failure handling, dependencies, design decisions, limitations | Context `flowchart`, component `flowchart`, one `sequenceDiagram` per key flow |
| `02-data-model.md` | Data Model | Domain model, persistent storage, schemas and contracts, lifecycle, tenancy | `classDiagram` or `erDiagram`; `erDiagram` for each SQL store |
| `03-messaging.md` | Messaging | Streams, subjects, consumers, KV buckets, payloads, delivery semantics, headers | Message-topology `flowchart LR`; message-lifecycle `sequenceDiagram` |
| `04-authentication.md` | Authentication & Authorization | Inbound authentication, authorization, tenancy, outbound credentials, secrets, security considerations | `sequenceDiagram` for inbound authentication and for outbound credential acquisition, where they apply |
| `05-api.md` | API Reference | GraphQL, HTTP and WebSocket endpoints, error model, health, compatibility | Request-pipeline `flowchart` when the service exposes an API |
| `06-configuration.md` | Configuration | Configuration sources, environment variables, files, dynamic configuration, startup validation | Configuration-sources `flowchart` |
| `07-operations.md` | Operations | Build and deployment, runtime topology, observability, scaling, runbooks, data repair | CI/CD `flowchart`; runtime-topology `flowchart` |
| `08-development.md` | Development & Testing | Prerequisites, layout, running locally, tests, tools, conventions, keeping docs current | None required |
| `09-glossary.md` | Glossary | Terms and abbreviations used in the documents (repository level only) | None |
| `10-documentation-standards.md` | Documentation Standards | This document (repository level only, generated) | None |

{{#single}}
The exact headings for each document are in the templates in [`templates/component/`](templates/component/) and [`templates/shared/`](templates/shared/).
{{/single}}

The exact headings for each service document are in [`templates/component/`](templates/component/). The repository-level documents use the same file names and titles, with headings suited to the platform view, from [`templates/platform/`](templates/platform/).

## 4. Page anatomy

Every standard document starts the same way:

{{#single}}
````markdown
# {{NAME}}: Architecture

[Overview](README.md) · **Architecture** · [Data model](02-data-model.md) · … · [Standards](10-documentation-standards.md)

> **Repository:** `{{REPO}}` · **Last verified against source:** 2026-01-31 (`{{BRANCH}}` @ `0000000`)
````
{{/single}}
{{#monorepo}}
````markdown
# <service>: Architecture

[Overview](README.md) · **Architecture** · [Data model](02-data-model.md) · … · [Platform docs](../../../docs/README.md)

> **Service:** `{{COMPONENTS_DIR}}/<service>` · **Last verified against source:** 2026-01-31 (`{{BRANCH}}` @ `0000000`)
````
{{/monorepo}}

{{#single}}
- **Title:** `# {{NAME}}: <title suffix>`, for example `# {{NAME}}: Messaging`.
{{/single}}
{{#monorepo}}
- **Title:** `# <service directory name>: <title suffix>`, for example `# example-service: Messaging`. Repository-level documents use `# {{NAME}}: <title suffix>`.
{{/monorepo}}
- **Navigation bar:** the line after the title links every document in the set, with the current page in bold and not linked. The scaffold writes it; keep it exactly as written.
{{#single}}
- **Metadata line:** the repository and the date and commit the content was last checked against the code. Update it whenever you re-verify a document.
{{/single}}
{{#monorepo}}
- **Metadata line:** the service path (or `all services in this monorepo` at the repository level) and the date and commit the content was last checked against the code. Update it whenever you re-verify a document.
{{/monorepo}}
- **Numbered H2 sections:** use exactly the H2 headings from the template, in the same order. Add H3 subsections as needed.
- **Sections that do not apply** keep their heading and say `_Not applicable._` followed by one sentence explaining why. A missing section is ambiguous; a "not applicable" section is information.
- **Template text:** replace every `<placeholder>` and delete the template's guidance comments. The check reports any that are left.

## 5. Writing conventions

| Topic | Convention |
|---|---|
| Tense and voice | Present tense, active voice, describing current behaviour. History belongs in git and in pull requests, not in the documents. |
| Names | Use the exact identifiers from code in backticks: streams (`EXAMPLE_INPUT`), subjects (`example.input`), environment variables (`NATS_URL`), GraphQL operations (`saveConfig`), roles (`Steward`). |
| Services | Refer to services by their directory or repository name. Introduce platform services once with their abbreviation, for example function-integrator (FI) and user-auth-service (UAS), and list every abbreviation in the [glossary](09-glossary.md). |
| Source references | Link files with relative links, for example to `../internal/config/config.go` from a service's `docs/`. Prefer files and functions over line numbers, which drift. |
| Configurable names | Give the default value and the variable that overrides it: `EXAMPLE_INPUT` (`NATS_STREAM_EXAMPLE_INPUT`). |
| Environment variable tables | Columns `Variable \| Required \| Default \| Description`. "Required" means the process refuses to start without it. Use `—` for no default. |
| Tables vs prose | Enumerations (operations, variables, streams, failure modes) go in tables. Explanations and rationale go in prose. |
| Examples | JSON payloads and GraphQL requests in fenced code blocks with a language tag. Use obviously fake identifiers (`00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000`, `example-customer`). |
| Secrets | Never include secret values, tokens, private keys or credentials. Name the secret and where it is stored. |
| Uncertainty | If the code does not settle a question, say what is known and what is not ("The replica count is set in `wanaware-infrastructure`"). Do not guess. |
| Emphasis | No emoji. Use bold sparingly for key terms on first use and for runbook labels. |

## 6. Diagram conventions

All diagrams are fenced ` ```mermaid ` blocks. Use only these diagram types, which GitHub renders reliably: `flowchart`, `sequenceDiagram`, `classDiagram`, `erDiagram`, `stateDiagram-v2`.

### 6.1 Shapes and styles

| Element | Notation | Example |
|---|---|---|
| The service being documented | Rectangle with class `focus` | `svc["example-service"]` and `class svc focus` |
| Other services in this repository | Rectangle | `other["other-service"]` |
| Platform services outside this repository | Rectangle with class `ext` (dashed) | `fi["function-integrator"]` and `class fi ext` |
| Data stores (PostgreSQL, Neo4j, Redis, GCS) | Cylinder | `pg[("PostgreSQL")]` |
| NATS streams, subjects and KV buckets | Hexagon | `s1{{"EXAMPLE_INPUT<br/>example.input"}}` |
| People and external actors | Stadium | `steward(["Steward"])` |
| Interactions | Labelled arrow | `svc -->|"GraphQL getConfig"| other` |

Declare the classes once per diagram, without colours so that diagrams read well in light and dark themes:

```text
classDef focus stroke-width:3px
classDef ext stroke-dasharray:4 3
```

### 6.2 Syntax rules

- Quote every label that contains spaces, punctuation or `<br/>`: `a["Label (detail)"]`.
- Use `<br/>` for line breaks; no other HTML.
- Do not use Mermaid keywords as node ids (`end`, `graph`, `subgraph`, `style`, `class`, `click` — `end` in any case), and avoid `o` or `x` as the first letter of an id directly after `--` (they become edge markers).
- No `%%{init}%%` directives, themes, colours, `click` handlers or icons.
- In `sequenceDiagram`, start with `autonumber`, declare participants with short aliases (`participant S as example-service`), and avoid `;` and `#` in message text.
- In `erDiagram`, attribute types are single words (`uuid`, `text`, `jsonb`, `timestamptz`) and keys are `PK`, `FK` or `UK`.
- Keep a diagram to what one screen can show. Split large flows into several diagrams.

The check enforces the diagram types, `autonumber`, and the ban on directives, `click`, `style` and colours. In CI, the Documentation workflow also renders every diagram in the documents a pull request changes, and fails on any that do not render.

## 7. Earlier documents and new designs

The numbered documents are the only maintained description of the system. Documents that precede them (ADRs, low-level designs, proposals, implementation guides, handovers and test reports) are removed once their content about the current system is in the standard documents and every code comment that cited them points at the standard documents. They remain in git history:

```bash
git log --diff-filter=D --name-only --oneline -- docs
```

| Kind of material | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| A significant decision and its rationale | The "Key design decisions" table in `01-architecture.md` |
| A design for work not yet built | The ticket or pull request that proposes it; once it ships, describe the result in the standard documents |
| Test evidence and reports | The pull request, in its QA Report section |
| How to use the files in a code directory (scripts, fixtures, schemas) | A short README next to those files that links to the standard documents for everything else |

{{#single}}
Code comments that point at documentation use the form `docs/03-messaging.md §3.1 (Section title)`, with paths relative to the repository root. Cite the section number and its title so a reader can find it even after renumbering.
{{/single}}
{{#monorepo}}
Code comments that point at documentation use the form `docs/03-messaging.md §3.1 (Section title)`. Paths are relative to the service directory; use `{{COMPONENTS_DIR}}/<other-service>/docs/…` for another service, and add "at the repository root" for repository-level documents. Cite the section number and its title so a reader can find it even after renumbering.
{{/monorepo}}

## 8. Keeping documentation current

Update documentation in the same pull request as the code change. Use the "Keeping these docs current" table in `08-development.md` to find the right document. As a minimum:

| When you change… | Update… |
|---|---|
| A NATS stream, subject, consumer, header or payload | `03-messaging.md`{{#monorepo}} of the service and, for cross-service changes, the repository-level `docs/03-messaging.md`{{/monorepo}} |
| A GraphQL operation, HTTP endpoint or error code | `05-api.md` (and `04-authentication.md` if its permissions change) |
| An environment variable or its default | `06-configuration.md` |
| A database migration, GCS layout or KV bucket | `02-data-model.md` |
| Roles, permissions, tenant rules or outbound credentials | `04-authentication.md`{{#monorepo}} of the service and the repository-level `docs/04-authentication.md`{{/monorepo}} |
| The deployment workflow, Dockerfile or runtime dependencies | `07-operations.md` |
{{#monorepo}}
| A new service | Follow [§9.2](#92-adding-a-new-service) |
{{/monorepo}}

### 8.1 Validation

Run the check from the repository root. It checks that every standard document exists with the template's title, navigation bar, metadata line and H2 headings; that no template placeholders or guidance comments are left; that relative links and anchors resolve; and that diagrams follow [§6](#6-diagram-conventions):

```bash
python3 docs/templates/docs_kit.py check
```

Check that Mermaid diagrams render before opening a pull request. Either preview the file on GitHub or in an editor with Mermaid support, or render it with the Mermaid CLI, which fails on the first invalid diagram:

```bash
npx -y -p @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli@11.12.0 mmdc -i docs/03-messaging.md -o /tmp/rendered.md
```

The Documentation workflow (`.github/workflows/documentation.yml`) runs the same check on every pull request through the shared `wanaware/.github` workflow `docs-check.yaml`, and renders the diagrams in the documents the pull request changes.

## 9. Tooling

The docs kit lives in [`wanaware/.github`]({{KIT_HOME}}). This repository keeps a copy in [`templates/`](templates/): the templates the check compares documents with, the checker itself, and `docs-kit.json` with this repository's settings (layout, name, services directory, branch named in metadata lines).

### 9.1 Scaffolding and refreshing

Running the Documentation workflow by hand (Actions → Documentation → Run workflow) opens a pull request that adds any missing standard document from the templates. It never overwrites a document that exists. With **refresh** selected it also replaces the kit's own files (`templates/`, this document) with the current version from `wanaware/.github`, so a change to the standard reaches this repository as a reviewable pull request. The same is available locally:

```bash
python3 docs/templates/docs_kit.py scaffold
```

To change the standard itself, such as a heading, a template or a rule here, change it in `wanaware/.github` and refresh, so every repository stays the same.

{{#monorepo}}
### 9.2 Adding a new service

1. Create `{{COMPONENTS_DIR}}/<service>/` and run `python3 docs/templates/docs_kit.py scaffold`. It adds the service's `docs/` from [`templates/component/`](templates/component/).
2. Replace every placeholder and delete the guidance comments.
3. Add a link to `docs/README.md` in the service's own `README.md`.
4. Add the service to the service tables in [`README.md`](README.md) (the check fails until it is linked there) and to the catalogs in the repository-level `01-architecture.md`, `03-messaging.md`, `04-authentication.md` and `05-api.md` as appropriate.
5. Run `python3 docs/templates/docs_kit.py check`.
{{/monorepo}}
